# Godot result attribution to the latest player request

The latest build in a session remains useful history. It does not prove that a
later player request changed, checked or applied anything. The main renderer's
creation status read includes the latest durable turn identity and whether the
build belongs to that request. Task IDs are derived from the host-owned session
and turn. Automatic repair may share a result only when both turns carry the
same exact host capture and world. Missing evidence stays unresolved.

A previous result is labelled as such. It cannot trigger automatic conversation
closure, automatic dialogue entry or a fresh completion announcement. The
model's original text remains intact, including interrupted partial replies.
This presentation does not classify ordinary questions as failed edits or
authorize a new model call. Normal retry and application permissions remain.

Targeted tests cover a prior applied build followed by an interrupted read-only
turn, current checks, capture-bound automatic repair, cross-world refusal and
unknown identity. Actual retained player data and a packaged continuation are
separate acceptance evidence from these deterministic checks.

Capture the active-turn start generation before the first asynchronous session
read and recheck it after every attribution read. The generation survives turn
completion, so a fast new request cannot disappear between those checks. An
active turn must also agree with the latest message's metric identity. The UI
records observing a running request even before any result read succeeds; its
first already-applied current result can still complete the automatic handoff.

## Actionable result feedback (2026-09-15)

Keep the existing PI desktop result card, overlay status and preview controls.
The host's phases and requirement-status fields are unchanged. A successful
automatic check, including a CPU/navigation probe, is not semantic gameplay
acceptance; an applied build only proves which version entered the world. Model
final prose and normal turn completion cannot promote either claim.

Use short states: Checking, Applying, Added to world / ready to try, and Needs
attention. A fresh ready candidate highlights Try preview and keeps Add to world
as a separate action. An applied current result offers Try in world through the
existing world surface and presentation mode. Failed/interrupted/history results
offer the existing checks surface. Missing candidates do not advertise an available
preview. Do not claim that progress was preserved solely from the applied phase.

Keep the automatic-check/playtest distinction in collapsed check details rather
than a long warning on every success card. Show errors as a short readable cause
with the exact original diagnostic available in a collapsed section. Unknown
errors remain explicit failures. This does not rewrite or hide the model's final
message, change checks, authorize another model request or replace player review.

During status refresh retain the same owner's last known card, mark confirmation
as pending and disable candidate/use actions until a fresh successful read. On a
failed read keep that record visibly unconfirmed. Session/world changes clear the
old card immediately and late replies/actions cannot act on or display errors for
the new owner. Preserve stale-source and current/previous/unresolved attribution
gates. An in-flight operation keeps its existing lock until completion without
labelling a new owner's result as applying.

Record observing an active model turn even while result reads are pending. Only
fresh matching automatic-application/runtime evidence may perform the existing
automatic play handoff; its Ask/full-workbench/live-draft/owner safeguards remain.
The status card has no invented progress percentage or independent task database.
